changes.motivation: The previous commit added lib.mapAttrs over config.systemd.timers inside a systemd.services definition, creating a cycle: NixOS systemd.nix validates timers by checking services, which triggers the services definition to read timers again. This caused infinite recursion on every build.
changes.summary: Removed RemainAfterExit = lib.mkDefault true from the systemd service submodule and removed the lib.mapAttrs ... config.systemd.timers override from modules/common/systemd/default.nix. Services that need RemainAfterExit must now set it explicitly.

changes.motivation: The docs described RemainAfterExit = true as a codebase default, which was no longer true after the fix. The initial doc update placed a RemainAfterExit note in the 'Codebase defaults' section, which was wrong since it is no longer a default.
changes.summary: Updated docs/modules/systemd-services/system.md: removed RemainAfterExit from the codebase defaults section and moved a warning about it (specifically that timer-paired services must not set it to true) into the timer-activated service section where it is contextually relevant.

problems: The commit that introduced the infinite recursion (fix(systemd): prevent timer-paired services from skipping reruns) used config.systemd.timers inside a config.systemd.services definition — a classic NixOS evaluation cycle that is easy to overlook. There is no guard or lint check to catch cross-referencing mutually-validating systemd options, and the error message (infinite recursion) does not point clearly to the location in the custom module, making diagnosis slower than it should be.
